profiles.meeting_scenario: A metropolitan pilot team is holding a planning meeting to prepare a six-week demonstration of a web-based 3D Land Administration workflow for a mixed-use redevelopment site above a rail corridor. The pilot is meant to show how BIM/IFC design data can be reused in a future 3D Land Administration System aligned with LADM concepts and shared across the spatial development lifecycle. The agenda is to agree on what the demo package will contain, how the source models will be prepared, which legal-space objects will be represented, who will produce each component, and what must be ready for the steering committee review at the end of the month. The expected outcome is an agreed plan for assembling the demonstration dataset, transforming the design information into land-administration-ready objects, and scheduling the review deliverables.

members.name: Elena Markovic
members.expertise: Land administration, cadastral modelling, LADM-based information design, cross-agency data governance
members.background: Elena leads a city innovation program exploring how legal spaces for stratified property, tunnels, and utility corridors can be represented in a future 3D LAS; she has spent most of her career in cadastral modernization projects and works closely with registry and planning offices.
members.private_state: She wants the pilot to look administratively credible to the registry and legal teams, avoid overcommitting to full legal validation, and show that municipal staff can reuse existing project data without building a bespoke modelling pipeline.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'the parcel model,' it naturally refers to the legal-space dataset that her office exported last quarter from the cadastral staging database, not the planning massing geometry used by the urban design team.

A 'review-ready' package means a steering-committee demonstration bundle: stable visuals, mapped LADM classes, and a few worked examples, not a submission-quality dataset suitable for statutory checking.

Preparing the IFC for reuse mainly means extracting and labeling bounded spaces that correspond to legal volumes and responsibility spaces, while keeping engineering detail outside scope unless it directly supports rights, restrictions, or responsibilities.

The 'site' for this pilot includes the air-rights podium, tower lots, basement retail, and the registered rail protection volume beneath, but not the broader utility network beyond the project boundary.

members.name: Ravi Deshpande
members.expertise: BIM/IFC workflows, model federation, CDE delivery, design-to-operations information exchange
members.background: Ravi has led several digital delivery programs for infrastructure and commercial developments, focusing on converting discipline models into coordinated IFC packages and setting up web-based viewers and data services for downstream reuse.
members.private_state: He wants the pilot to demonstrate that the BIM delivery stack can already feed public-sector systems with minimal remodelling, and he is trying to avoid manual reinterpretation work that would make the workflow look fragile or expensive.
hidden_assumptions: When people mention 'the parcel model,' they mean the current federated design context model used by the redevelopment project team, because that is the geometry everyone is actively coordinating against.

A 'review-ready' deliverable means the package should be clean enough that technical reviewers could rerun the transformation and inspect the source-to-output traceability, even if minor presentation polish is missing.

Preparing the IFC for reuse means publishing the coordinated federation with agreed property sets, levels, and discipline references intact so downstream users can derive what they need without recasting the authoring model.

The 'site' naturally includes connecting access structures and utility diversions shown in the federated project model, because those are part of the constructed development envelope even if they cross cadastral boundaries.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the parcel model
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the parcel model' as the base geometry they will align the demo to.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the municipal cadastral staging export containing legal parcel and volumetric boundary primitives for the pilot area.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ravi means the redevelopment team's federated planning/design context model that includes parcel extents, setbacks, and surrounding structures.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both datasets cover the same site and are routinely described internally as the parcel model, so each hears a familiar phrase and assumes the other is pointing to the same digital artifact.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the end-of-month package must be 'review-ready.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena believes review-ready means fit for executive and registry stakeholder review: coherent examples, understandable legal-space narratives, and no glaring conceptual gaps.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ravi believes review-ready means technically reproducible and auditable by data reviewers, with stable IDs, transformation logs, and enough completeness for rerun testing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Review-ready sounds like a routine milestone label; both assume their professional standard is the obvious one, and neither expects the other to be using a materially different threshold under the same phrase.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Ravi will 'prepare the IFC for reuse in the 3D LAS workflow.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes this covers extracting only the spaces and surfaces needed to instantiate legal volumes, common-property zones, and restriction areas relevant to land administration.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ravi assumes this covers publishing the full coordinated IFC federation with discipline structure and property sets preserved, leaving any legal abstraction to later mapping steps.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds operational rather than strategic, and both see their interpretation as a normal preprocessing step rather than a decision requiring explicit negotiation.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss showing the workflow 'for the whole site' so the demo feels realistic.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the cadastral pilot footprint plus the subsurface rail protection volume that directly affects rights and restrictions inside the redevelopment lots.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ravi means the broader federated development extent, including utility diversions and access links just outside the cadastral lots because they appear in the coordinated project model.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use 'whole site' as if the boundary is self-evident from the project name, but each inherits a different boundary from their home system and professional practice.

turns.inner_thought: I need to frame this as a credible land-administration demonstration, not a promise of legal validation. For end of month, review-ready means something the steering committee and registry people can understand: stable visuals, clear LADM mappings, and a few convincing cases showing the mixed-use stack over the rail corridor. If we keep the scope disciplined, we can show reuse of existing data without creating a custom modelling effort.
